articles.title: Self-Building Labs
articles.summary: Self-driving laboratories (SDLs) accelerate scientific discovery by automating experimental execution and optimization. AI agents can increasingly propose new experiments, but existing SDLs can only run the procedures they were built for. Adapting them to a new experiment still takes extensive manual engineering, which makes laboratory flexibility the bottleneck for scaling discovery. We introduce the self-building laboratory (SBL), which designs, configures, and operates its own laboratory setup given a high-level scientific goal. articles.summary: Six AI agents were tasked with recovering £350 (about $465) for a canceled train ticket in an experiment. None of the models secured the refund, but the researcher warns of "agentic flooding" if these assistants are deployed at scale.
